Crypto Idea

The boldest experiment in crypto

Michael Saylor, the founder of Strategy, the world's largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, has come up with something unique.

Instead of simply buying Bitcoin with the company's own money, he's building an entire financial machine that attracts outside capital and channels it into BTC purchases.

One of these instruments is STRC. Investors provide capital to the company and receive regular payouts of around 11.5% annually. The company then uses that capital to buy Bitcoin. But there's a catch.

⚙️ How it’s supposed to work

STRC — an instrument Saylor designed with the help of AI — is intended to keep its price hovering around $100.

If the price falls, the company raises the yield to attract more buyers. The price is supposed to recover. Think of it as an automatic stabilizer.

❓ Why this is interesting 

Right now, STRC is trading at roughly $83, despite its $100 target value. The yield has already been increased, but the market isn't responding the way the model was designed to.

This is the first real stress test of the entire structure. If the mechanism fails to stabilize the price, the company will either have to keep increasing payouts to investors or buy less Bitcoin.

Saylor is essentially testing one question: can financial instruments be built around a single asset indefinitely?

An open-source coding model has been released that outperforms Claude Opus 4.7 on key benchmarks

DeepReinforce has released Ornith-1.0, a family of open-source models tailored for agent encoding. There are four variants: 9B Dense, 31B Dense, 35B MoE, and 397B MoE. Based on Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5.

The key idea of the model is that it learns not only to solve tasks but also to build scenarios for their solutions. Conventional models receive a ready-made "framework" of how to approach the task and work with it. Ornith generates and improves it during the training process.

The flagship 397B version scored 77.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 82.4 on SWE-Bench Verified. Claude Opus 4.7 on the same tests shows 70.3 and 80.8.

The 35B version outperforms Qwen 3.5-397B on Terminal-Bench, meaning a model eleven times smaller in parameters works better on this test.

The 9B variant, which runs on regular hardware, outperforms Gemma 4-31B on several benchmarks.

All models are available on Hugging Face.

Main Points
⏺ Flash loans let users borrow assets instantly with no collateral, if repaid in one transaction.
⏺ They enable arbitrage, refinancing, and liquidation strategies.
⏺ Powerful but often exploited in DeFi hacks.

1️⃣ Instant credit — Loans are granted and repaid within a single block.
2️⃣ Arbitrage — Traders exploit price differences across exchanges risk-free.
3️⃣ Debt restructuring — Users shift positions across protocols with one transaction.
4️⃣ Exploits — Many DeFi hacks used flash loans to manipulate markets.
5️⃣ Innovation — Despite risks, flash loans remain a unique tool only possible on blockchain.

Final Thoughts

Flash loans show both the creativity and the dangers of DeFi. Used well, they’re brilliant — abused, they can cause multi-million dollar exploits.
